# Results — Study 682 (Inverse-Fisher-RSI)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**Ehlers' Inverse Fisher Transform of RSI turns a mushy oscillator into a crisp -1/+1 signal
with cleaner overbought/oversold turns** than plain RSI. Offline & deterministic once cached;
run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily total-return closes (`auto_adjust=True`), 6 tickers, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, 4,147 rows each |
| Universe | SPY, QQQ, IWM, AAPL, MSFT, NVDA — same basket as sibling [669-rsi-divergence](../../669-rsi-divergence/) |
| Fingerprints | SPY `0c6ad198f447` · QQQ `a84e44862578` · IWM `f0b7b205c2af` · AAPL `8699fe541146` · MSFT `51aba9472a5f` · NVDA `454a3ad24423` |
| Indicator | `IFT-RSI = tanh(WMA(0.1*(RSI(5)-50), 9))`, Ehlers' exact recipe (TASC 2002 / *Cybernetic Analysis*, 2004) |
| Signals | **IFT-RSI bullish** = cross UP through -0.5; **IFT-RSI bearish** = cross DOWN through +0.5; baselines: plain RSI(14) cross up 30 / down 70, plain RSI(2) cross up 10 (Connors-style) |
| Statistics | Welch *t* for the pooled signal-vs-unconditional split; **Newey-West (lags = horizon)** *t* on the pooled dummy regression as the overlap-robust cross-check; Wilson interval on hit rate; 20-seed × 200-draw random-signal placebo |
| Execution / costs | one documented execution lag: signal known at close *t*, forward return earned from close *t+1* to close *t+1+h* (a single shift); timer costs = 2 × one-way cost × NAV per round trip (5 / 10 bps) |
| No survivorship | SPY/QQQ/IWM are baskets, not survivor panels; the five single names are current mega-caps, named as a **selection-not-survivorship** convenience sample (no delisted/failed names in the universe by construction) — the same caveat sibling 669 carries |

## The headline — IFT-RSI bullish cross (-0.5) forward return vs unconditional

| horizon | signal mean | unconditional mean | gap | Welch *t* | NW *t* | hit rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5d | +23.8 bps (n=710) | +39.7 bps (n=24,136) | **-15.9 bps** | -1.07 | -1.09 | 58.3% (Wilson [54.6%, 61.9%]) |
| 10d | +40.3 bps (n=707) | +80.2 bps (n=24,109) | **-39.9 bps** | **-1.89** | **-2.05** | 56.9% (Wilson [53.2%, 60.5%]) |
| 20d | +179.0 bps (n=706) | +159.8 bps (n=24,050) | +19.3 bps | +0.65 | +0.77 | 68.0% (Wilson [64.5%, 71.3%]) |

No horizon clears the desk's **t ≥ 2** bar *in support of the claim*. The one number that gets
close — 10-day NW *t* = **-2.05** — points the **wrong way**: buying an IFT-RSI oversold snap
back through -0.5 earned *less* than simply holding any random day in this basket, not more.
The sign flips again at 20 days (mildly positive, still nowhere near significant). That
inconsistency across horizons is itself evidence against a real, stable effect.

**Random-signal placebo (20 seeds × 200 draws, h=10d):** observed signal mean +40.3 bps vs a
placebo mean of **+79.8 bps** (sd 20.0) over 4,000 draws of random-but-matched-count entries
→ **p = 0.9710** — 97% of random entry sets of the same size *beat* the actual IFT-RSI signal.
The "oversold bounce" entry is a *worse*-than-average entry, not a better one.

## Bearish-cross check — IFT-RSI cross DOWN through +0.5 (should predict *weaker* returns)

| horizon | signal mean | unconditional mean | gap | Welch *t* | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5d | +39.4 bps (n=886) | +39.3 bps | +0.1 bps | +0.01 | +0.01 |
| 10d | +79.5 bps (n=886) | +79.0 bps | +0.5 bps | +0.03 | +0.03 |
| 20d | +115.5 bps (n=881) | +162.0 bps | -46.4 bps | -1.82 | -2.17 |

The "overbought" side is even flatter than the bullish side at short horizons — a bearish
IFT-RSI reading tells you almost nothing about the next 5–10 days — and only shows a
(borderline, still uncertified two-ways-out-of-three) drag at 20 days. Symmetric non-result.

## The comparison — does IFT-RSI beat plain RSI(14) / RSI(2) reversal? (h=10d)

| signal | n | gap vs unconditional | Welch *t* | NW *t* | hit rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **IFT-RSI bull (-0.5 cross)** | 707 | **-39.9 bps** | -1.89 | -2.05 | 56.9% |
| plain RSI(14) bull (cross up 30) | 189 | -54.0 bps | -1.08 | -1.01 | 56.6% |
| plain RSI(2) bull (cross up 10, Connors) | 1,354 | **+20.8 bps** | +1.36 | +1.53 | 61.0% |

Ehlers' transform does **not** sharpen anything here: IFT-RSI and plain RSI(14) both land on
the *negative* side of unconditional (neither certified), while the simplest baseline of all —
Connors' RSI(2), the subject of sibling [75-knee-jerk](../../75-knee-jerk/) — is the only one
with a *positive* (still sub-bar) tilt. Signal counts also show the "crisper, fewer whipsaws"
claim is only half right: IFT-RSI fires far less often than RSI(2) (707 vs 1,354) — fewer,
"cleaner-looking" crosses — but *more* often than RSI(14) (189), and none of that frequency
difference buys any edge.

## Third axis — a timer with costs

Long-flat: enter on the IFT-RSI bullish cross, exit on the bearish cross; pooled across the
six-ticker basket, 2010-2026 (one of the strongest sustained equity bull runs on record).

| cost | net Sharpe | buy-and-hold Sharpe | ann. return net | ann. return buy-and-hold | exposure |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 bps | **+0.48** | +0.71 | +8.68%/yr | +19.86%/yr | 47.8% |
| 10 bps | +0.45 | +0.71 | +8.13%/yr | +19.86%/yr | 47.8% |

**Random-exposure control** (20 seeds, an i.i.d. Bernoulli(47.8%) long-flat mask, same
time-in-market, same 5 bps costs): mean Sharpe **+0.35** (sd 0.10) → **z = +1.27** (real Sharpe
beats only 16/20 random seeds). The timer sits *below* buy-and-hold by construction (it is out
of the market 52% of the time during a historic bull run) and only weakly, uncertifiably, beats
a coin-flip timer with the same exposure.

For reference, the RSI(14) timer (cross up 30 / down 70) is worse still: net Sharpe **+0.31**
(5 bps), **+5.41%/yr**, 30.3% exposure — neither "sharper" indicator produces anything close to
an investable timing rule.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic AR(1) log-return process, `r_t = mu + rho*(mu - r_{t-1}) + eps_t`; the planted
reversion operates at a single 1-day lag, so the machinery check runs the identical Welch split
at **h=1** (where the effect actually lives), not at the headline h=5/10/20.

| world | Welch *t* (h=1) |
|---|--:|
| null (rho=0, random walk), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.07** (sd 0.87), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted rho=0.6 (seed 682) | signal +39.9 bps vs base +2.7 bps → **+3.81** |

The detector never fires on a random walk and lights up cleanly on genuine planted
mean-reversion. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the
real-tape stamp; note it also confirms the real-tape null result at h=5/10/20 is not an
artefact of an underpowered pipeline — the same code finds a much smaller planted effect at
the horizon where it actually exists.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** No horizon clears **t ≥ 2** in support of the claim; the closest call
  (10-day NW *t* = -2.05) runs the *wrong direction* — IFT-RSI oversold entries underperform
  the basket's own unconditional forward return, and 97% of random-signal placebo draws beat
  the real signal (p = 0.9710). The bearish side is a near-total non-result too.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The long-flat timer nets a Sharpe of +0.48 (5 bps), well below
  simple buy-and-hold (+0.71) over the same 2010-2026 window, and only weakly beats a
  random-exposure timer matched on time-in-market (z = +1.27, not certified).
- **"Sharper turning points than plain RSI(2/14)"? — BUSTED.** IFT-RSI's own forward-return
  gap (-39.9 bps, t=-1.89) is worse than plain RSI(2)'s (+20.8 bps, t=+1.36) and no better than
  plain RSI(14)'s (-54.0 bps, t=-1.08); the timer built on it loses to the RSI(14) timer on
  exposure-adjusted terms and to buy-and-hold outright. The Fisher-transform math produces a
  visually crisper oscillator — bounded, snappy, easy to eyeball — but crisper-looking is not
  more informative.
